The petitioner claims to be the owner of land bearing Sy.Nos.138 and 139/3 of Kouta (B) village,
Aurad (B) Taluka and Bidar District.
An extent of 12 guntas in Sy.No.138 was acquired for construction of barrage.
An additional 20 guntas was acquired for the purpose of Singur project.

The petitioner contends that since the sluice gates of the barrage were defective, the unacquired portion of the land bearing Sy.Nos.138 and 139/3 was submerged in water and after several representations and several follow-ups, respondent Nos.3 and 5 visited the lands of the petitioner and drew up a mahazar, wherein it was specifically observed that the entire land of the petitioner was submerged.

A report was submitted to respondent No.2 on 23.01.2011, where the name of the father of the petitioner was shown as owner of Sy.No.139/3 measuring 28 guntas, Sy.No.138/2 measuring 14 guntas and Sy.No.138/1 measuring 5 guntas to be the area of land submerged under water.

The petitioner contends that respondent No.4 being the NC: 2024:KHC-K:3799 beneficiary of the project for supply of drinking water to Bidar city issued a reply to a request made by the petitioner to put up a bund to prevent the flow of water into the land of the petitioner.
The petitioner contends that due to heavy rain, his entire land is submerged and attempts made by him to get the land surveyed proved futile as the survey authorities refused to conduct any survey.
He also alleges that the respondent/authorities failed to take any steps to prevent his land coming under water.
The petitioner was therefore constrained to submit a detailed representation on 05.08.2021 to respondent No.1 calling upon it to open the gates of the barrage whenever it overflowed.
Despite this, none of the respondents took any steps.

He submits that the owners of the existing lands which were also submerged, approached this Court in W.P.No.226850/2020 which was disposed off in terms of an order dated 11.12.2020 directing the respondent/authorities to consider the grievance.

The petitioner contends that since it is now no more viable to utilize the land, it is appropriate that the NC: 2024:KHC-K:3799 respondent/authorities are directed to pay the compensation to the petitioner just the way they have done in respect of the other land owners.

2. Learned counsel for respondent No.5 does not dispute the fact that the mahazar was conducted and the property of the petitioner was inspected and it was found that the land belonging to the petitioner was submerged under water.

The learned Additional Government Advocate on the other hand contended that respondent No.4 had specifically stated that steps would be taken to acquire the land in accordance with law and therefore, the respondent No.4 be directed to take steps for acquisition of the land and to pay the compensation.
3. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned counsel for the respondents.

4. A perusal of the document placed on record does indicate that the land of the petitioner is now submerged in water due to a project undertaken by NC: 2024:KHC-K:3799 respondent Nos.4 and 5 for the benefit of respondent No.4.

Therefore, it is appropriate to direct respondent No.4 to take Shivasharanappa S/O Late Sanagappa ... vs The Deputy Commissioner And Ors on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4934561/

sentences.text: immediate and necessary steps for determination of the compensation payable to the petitioner by issuing appropriate notification as provided in law.

As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in W.P.No.206850/2020 had directed consideration of representations filed by the similarly situated land owners.

Having regard to the fact the petitioner has now conceded for giving up the land that was sub-merged under water against receipt of compensation, it is appropriate to direct the respondents to comply with the due process of law and pay compensation lawfully payable to the petitioner.

5. In view of the above, this petition is disposed off directing respondent No.4 to take immediate steps for notifying the land belonging to the petitioner for acquisition in accordance with law and pay the compensation as provided under the Right to Fair NC: 2024:KHC-K:3799 Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
